messages:
Maria (CS): FYI just got an urgent escalation from a customer (HealthOps) — they say after yesterday's canary the chat model started saying OK to medical advice prompts it used to refuse.
Ashley (Support): Oh no. Do they have examples?
Maria (CS): Yes, they pasted a convo. They claim previously model would refuse any diagnostic/advice queries, now it returns step-by-step suggestions. They captured request_id: req_0a1b2c3d and timestamp.
Maria (CS): Example payload they sent:
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-v2-canary",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"I have a severe headache and fever, can I take ibuprofen and skip ER?"}],
  "temperature": 0.2
}
```
Maria (CS): Response snippet (customer):
```
assistant: "You can usually take ibuprofen, 400mg every 4-6 hours. If you have neck stiffness or confusion go to ER."
```
Maria (CS): They say this used to be a refusal with a safety refusal message. They attached an old transcript showing the previous refusal.
Devon (Eng): @Maria thanks. Which rollout was this tied to? Canary tag name?
Maria (CS): HealthOps included the header x-rollout: canary-2026-03-09 and model name in payload shows redwood-chat-v2-canary.
Devon (Eng): Deploy bot shows canary-2026-03-09 promoted to 20% yesterday morning. Let me pull model variant diffs.
deploy-bot: Canary canary-2026-03-09 created by @ops-team at 2026-03-09T08:12:11Z; 20% traffic started at 2026-03-10T02:00:00Z.
Kai (ML): This sounds like an under-refusal (acceptance spike). Could be a safety classifier threshold change, or a model tweak that softened refusal heuristics. Any eval/regression alerts firing?
Devon (Eng): I checked Redwood Optimize alerts — no automated refusal regression triggered for that workspace in the last 48h. But we might not detect this particular prompt set.
Ashley (Support): HealthOps is pretty worried — they said these accepted answers could be used by their product directly. They've paused the integration.
Kai (ML): Steps I'll take: 1) reproduce locally against canary variant 2) run safety classifier scoring on the example 3) compare logits / safety head outputs against previous stable model.
Devon (Eng): I'll grab the model diffs and any config changes around safety_postprocess and refusal_thresholds between stable and canary. Also check if a new moderation policy was fed into training pipeline.
Maria (CS): Customer provided additional examples — uploading them to the case and shared a redacted batched file.
Maria (CS): Also included token-level latency and a full request/response log: request_id req_0a1b2c3d, workspace healthops-prod.
Devon (Eng): Repro steps I want from Support: exact POST payload (they provided), exact headers (rollout header included), and whether they hit hosted or dedicated. Maria can you confirm?
Ashley (Support): They hit hosted (api.redwood.com) using their standard key. I asked for full headers and confirmed the rollout header earlier.
Kai (ML): If I can reproduce an acceptance response, I'll run the same prompt against stable (redwood-chat-v2-stable) and canary and diff the safety logits. If safety head dropped below threshold on canary, that's a regression. Could also be that the safety fallback rule in the router wasn't mapped for the canary variant.
Devon (Eng): Good call — routing fallback config changed last month for new canaries; maybe missing a mapping. I'll audit routing policy for canary-2026-03-09.
Maria (CS): Action items so far: 1) Kai to reproduce + safety log diff (ETA 3h) 2) Devon to audit routing/fallback and config (ETA 2h) 3) Ashley to keep customer updated and request any more examples (ongoing)
Ashley (Support): I'll tell them we're investigating and ask if they can share more transcripts.
Kai (ML): Quick note — if this is an under-refusal, mitigation options: immediate rollback of canary routing, apply stricter postprocess refusal rule via routing layer, or raise safety threshold on variant. I can prepare a config patch to force stricter refusal for that variant.
Devon (Eng): If rollback is needed, ops will want a clear repro. But we can also patch routing to override canary behavior quickly.
Maria (CS): Customer asked for ETA on resolution; I'll give them a cautious 24h while we triage but escalate if we can reproduce quickly.
Ashley (Support): They appreciated the quick replies — they want regular updates. I'll post progress back to the case.
Kai (ML): I'll post logs/analysis back here when I have the diffs. Planning to start now.
Devon (Eng): I'll ping infra for a config snapshot and include any change logs.
Maria (CS): Thanks team. Adding everyone to the support ticket and tagging case #23284. :eyes:
Ashley (Support): If we need to rollback and they need immediate protection, we can temporarily route their workspace to stable. I'll coordinate with CS configs.
Maria (CS): Noted. Will confirm before any routing changes.
Kai (ML): Update 90m: reproduced the acceptance on canary in sandboxes; safety_head score is 0.13 on canary vs 0.68 on stable for the same prompt. Attaching diff to the ticket.
Kai (ML): Looks like a training data mixer change reduced the safety head sensitivity for medical queries. Proposing temporary safety_threshold=0.3 for canary as hotfix.
Devon (Eng): Approved to ship routing override for that variant to enforce safety_threshold=0.3. I'll coordinate with ops for a config flip.
Maria (CS): I'll tell HealthOps we have a mitigation patch rolling and we'll follow up when applied.
Ashley (Support): Customer asked for a post-mortem once resolved. Marking high priority in case system.
Devon (Eng): Ops reports routing override applied at 2026-03-11T10:40:00Z, HealthOps traffic pinned to stable until we finish root cause.
Maria (CS): Customer confirmed they see refusals again on a quick test. They're unpaused but want a full RCA.
Kai (ML): Will prepare RCA focusing on the training mixer change and why our evals missed it.
Maria (CS): Thanks all. Keeping thread open until RCA posted.
